newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Tory chief quits, citing private life.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Tory chief quits, citing private life.

text.p: A leading member of Britain's embattled Conservative Party resigned his party post on Saturday, just weeks before the May 1 general election, citing problems in his personal life.
Sir Michael Hirst, chairman of the Conservative Party in Scotland, said in a letter to Prime Minister John Major that he was stepping down rather than embarrass the party.
Hirst's letter, which was broadcast on national radio, said:
"I very deeply regret these circumstances which have caused great distress to my family and which may, I fear, cause embarrassment to the party in the current climate."

The Conservative Party is beset by allegations of "sleaze" which have diverted it from its main campaign thrust of attacking the opposition Labour Party, given by a string of opinion polls as the likely runaway winner.

One member of parliament is resisting pressure to step down over allegations of an affair with a 17-year-old night club hostess. Another denies that he accepted cash in return for placing questions before Britain's parliament.
